items.title: Add cluster_blocked() + shared dep-graph helpers + Jaccard clustering (CLU)
items.description:
Add the deterministic systemic-cause clustering substrate to scripts/forge-session.py. Full Python is in spec 06-clustering-and-topology.md §2; follow it. Pure, stdlib-only, no class.

1. Add `import math` to the module import block (needed by item 004; add it here since CLU lands first).
2. Add CLUSTER_JACCARD_THRESHOLD: Final[float] = 0.5 (module-level, with the other Finals).
3. Add the shared dependency-graph helpers (used by both this item and item 004's compute_topology): _id_key (numeric ids sort numerically, else lexically after the numeric block), _build_dep_index (drops edges to ids not in the backlog), _transitive_dependents (memoized, cycle-safe DFS closure).
4. Add clustering: _ID_SHAPED_TOKEN regex, _normalize_reason (lowercase, split on non-alphanumeric, drop pure-number ^\d+$ and id-shaped ^[a-z]*\d+$ tokens, return the token SET), _jaccard (two empty sets → 0.0), and cluster_blocked (union-find over status=="blocked" items whose pairwise Jaccard >= CLUSTER_JACCARD_THRESHOLD; process in _id_key order; root component at lowest member id; emit sorted by lowest member id; each cluster carries clusterId="c"+lowest member id, memberIds, memberReasons, sharedTokens, and gatedIds/gatedCount = union of members' gated subtrees minus the members).
5. Create tests/test_decision_clustering.py per spec 07 §7.2. CRITICAL (V-015): vendor the three real verify-test-debt blockedReason strings VERBATIM into the test file (do not read them from any .rauf archive) and assert they cluster into exactly ONE candidate; add a comment recording the measured Jaccard margin (~0.028 over the 0.5 threshold) so a future threshold change that would re-split the incident is caught. Also cover: normalization drops number/id-shaped tokens; Jaccard boundary (exactly 0.5 clusters, just below does not); union-find transitivity (A~B, B~C, A≁C → one cluster); determinism across shuffled input; and that two genuinely distinct causes do NOT merge (under-clustering ok, over-clustering not).
6. Run `python3 scripts/build-adapters.py` and commit adapters/**.
acceptanceCriteria: import math is present; CLUSTER_JACCARD_THRESHOLD == 0.5 is a module-level Final
cluster_blocked and the _id_key/_build_dep_index/_transitive_dependents/_normalize_reason/_jaccard helpers are module-level flat functions (no class), stdlib-only

cluster_blocked output matches 00 §8.3 shape; clusterId == "c"+lowest member id; gatedIds/gatedCount = union of members' gated subtrees minus members; output is deterministic across shuffled input (all ordering via _id_key)
Normalization drops pure-number and id-shaped tokens (42, req12, t7); comparison is over the token set; two empty sets score 0.0 and never cluster
Jaccard boundary: a pair at exactly 0.5 clusters, a pair just below does not; union-find transitivity yields one cluster {A,B,C}
V-015: the three vendored blockedReason strings cluster into exactly one candidate; a comment records the measured Jaccard margin; two distinct causes do NOT merge
tests/test_decision_clustering.py passes; python3 scripts/build-adapters.py run and adapters/** committed; bash scripts/validate.sh passes
items.notes: CLU lands before TOPO (01 §4 steps 6-7); both reuse the §2.1 helpers, so those helpers land here. Under-clustering is the deliberately-chosen failure direction — the agent holds merge authority, the scripted floor must never over-merge. CLUSTER_JACCARD_THRESHOLD is falsifiable against the incident via the vendored V-015 fixture.
